concerns.concern: Pulse-induced heating followed by a thermal quench is not excluded. Contact and flux-flow dissipation could exceed the fridge cooling power. The turn-off-rate, temperature and ms-timescale arguments are all also consistent with a heat-then-quench mechanism. Contact resistances, dissipated energy, on-sample thermometry, a heater-only pulse and a pure temperature-quench control are requested.
concerns.quote: Heating and thermal quench are not excluded, and the two main counter-arguments do not exclude them.

concerns.concern: The work ignores well-established history-dependent J_c and memory effects in conventional vortex matter near the peak effect (NbSe2, CeRu2, V3Si, YBCO). The authors' own data show a peak-effect-like anomaly. The Bean-model argument does not address dynamic-ordering or edge-contamination scenarios.
concerns.quote: The relation to known vortex-matter metastability and memory effects is not addressed.

concerns.concern: The authors should identify which observations, if any, require two vortex species or SC1/SC2 coexistence rather than a generic vortex order–disorder transition. Discriminating tests are requested: J_ex scaling with J_c(B), edge and contact geometry dependence, and a benchmark on a conventional peak-effect material.
concerns.quote: Identify which observations, if any, require two vortex species or SC1/SC2 coexistence rather than a generic order–disorder vortex transition near a J_c anomaly.

concerns.concern: Linking the memory region to SC1/SC2 coexistence ('SC1.5') is not supported. In S2 the effect occurs at 7–14 T, well below the ~20 T boundary and the 15–20 T coexistence window.
concerns.quote: The identification of the memory region with SC1/SC2 coexistence ("SC1.5") is not established by the data.

concerns.concern: The SC1/SC2 phase boundaries and T_c(B, θ) are not measured on the samples used; the phase diagrams shown are only schematics. The memory region should be mapped against measured boundaries in normalised variables.
concerns.quote: No independent determination of the SC1/SC2 boundary is given for S1 or S2

concerns.concern: The disappearance of the effect near 19–20° could reflect the angle dependence of the reduced field B/B_c2(θ) and of the irreversibility field, rather than leaving the region below SC2. A field sweep at θ ≈ 25–30° is requested.
concerns.quote: could reflect this rather than leaving the region "below SC2".

concerns.concern: The field window differs between samples and is attributed to crystal quality. If disorder sets the window, that points to a pinning-controlled effect rather than an intrinsic one.
concerns.quote: If the field window is set by disorder, that itself points to a pinning-controlled phenomenon.

concerns.concern: The pulse-delta measurement mode may itself apply many abrupt turn-offs during a 'smooth' sweep. This contradicts the statement that all excitations were dc and blurs the distinction between pump and erase. Pulse parameters are requested, and a check with a truly continuous dc ramp.
concerns.quote: A "smooth" sweep may therefore itself contain many abrupt turn-offs.

concerns.concern: The reported 10 µs pulse durations and fast turn-off rates may not actually reach the sample through filtered dilution-fridge wiring. The filter configuration and oscilloscope traces of the delivered current are requested.
concerns.quote: These are delivered through dilution-fridge wiring that normally includes RC or π filters with kHz-scale cutoffs.

concerns.concern: The 2 mA erase steps are abrupt and comparable to the J_ex write threshold, which conflicts with treating erase as slow.
concerns.quote: The erase steps of 2 mA (~1 A cm⁻²) are abrupt steps comparable to the J_ex threshold

concerns.concern: The protocol drawn in Fig. 1d/e shows erase as a rectangular block that ends abruptly, which contradicts the main-text definition of erase as a slow ramp.
concerns.quote: This contradicts the main-text definition of erase as a slow ramp.

concerns.concern: The claim that the state persists for several hours (non-volatility) has no supporting data. Retention-versus-time data, the effect of repeated reads, the effect of small field or temperature excursions, and survival under thermal cycling are requested.
concerns.quote: The non-volatility and long-retention claim has no data behind it.

concerns.concern: The state is described inconsistently: 'metastable' in the Abstract, 'not transiently metastable' on p. 7, and a 'long-lived transient (metastable) state' in Methods.
concerns.quote: Wording is inconsistent

concerns.concern: A full V(J) read that exceeds J_c erases the state, so readout is destructive unless restricted to sub-critical currents.
concerns.quote: readout is destructive unless restricted to sub-critical J.

concerns.concern: Sample statistics are thin. Only S1 and S2 show the effect, and it is unclear whether the protocol was applied to the cleanest sample, S3. Results after thermal cycling are not shown.
concerns.quote: Sample statistics are thin

concerns.concern: No error bars are given anywhere. The run-to-run scatter of the equilibrium V(J) should be compared with ΔJ.
concerns.quote: No error bars are given anywhere (Figs. 2, 4e,f; ED Fig. 1).

concerns.concern: ΔJ magnitudes at nominally similar conditions differ between figures and the text. ΔJ needs a unique definition: reference curve, voltage criterion, averaging and noise floor.
concerns.quote: Inconsistent magnitudes at nominally similar conditions

concerns.concern: The sample cross-section dimensions, their uncertainty, and the uniformity of current flow between spot-welded contacts are not given.
concerns.quote: Give the cross-section dimensions, their uncertainty, and whether current flow is uniform between spot-welded contacts.

concerns.concern: There is no direct evidence that the vortex configuration changes; the state is defined only by a transport J_c shift. Requested tests include local versus distant voltage contacts, a force-free geometry, ac susceptibility or Campbell response, and noise spectroscopy.
concerns.quote: There is no direct evidence that the vortex configuration changes.

concerns.concern: The ~0.6 K closing temperature is called surprising by comparison with the zero-field T_c of 2.1 K, whereas T_c(B) at 14–20 T is much lower. It should be compared with T_c(B) and the irreversibility boundary at the same field.
concerns.quote: The temperature scale is compared with the wrong T_c.

concerns.concern: The RSJ model is under-specified and internally inconsistent. Parameters are missing or hand-chosen, temperature does not enter, and the γ range conflicts with the ED Fig. 2a colour bar. All parameters, and which features are inputs versus outputs, are requested.
concerns.quote: The RSJ model is under-specified, internally inconsistent and largely post hoc.

concerns.concern: Mapping a mm-scale bulk crystal with flux flow onto a single macroscopic phase is not justified. φ is used ambiguously, and a phase-modulated state is not obviously a grid of domain walls.
concerns.quote: Mapping a mm-scale bulk crystal with flux flow onto a single macroscopic phase is not justified.

concerns.concern: The key model result, that a quench lands in φ = π, is built in by placing large damping at π.
concerns.quote: The key result, that a quench lands in φ = π, is engineered by placing large damping at π.

concerns.concern: The model predicts lower flux-flow resistance in the memory state, but the measured curves merge at high J. At least one quantitative, falsifiable comparison is requested, along with temperature-dependent noise to test the T dependence.
concerns.quote: The measured curves instead merge at high J (Fig. 1c; ED Fig. 1).

concerns.concern: Technological claims are overstated. The 7–20 T, sub-0.4 K operating conditions are not stated plainly, the write energy is not quantified, and the pW scaling argument ignores contacts and assumes the effect persists in micron-scale devices.
concerns.quote: The technological claims are overstated.

concerns.concern: The AI-energy framing in the introduction is disproportionate to a bulk, high-field, millikelvin observation. Ref. 59 does not support the comparison made.
concerns.quote: The AI-energy framing in the introduction is disproportionate to a bulk, high-field, millikelvin observation.

concerns.concern: The analogy to the intrinsic diode effect does not discriminate between mechanisms and should be toned down.
concerns.quote: The analogy to the intrinsic diode effect (ref. 49) does not discriminate between mechanisms and should be toned down.

concerns.concern: The heating analysis and Figs. S2 and S7 are in Supplementary Information that was not available for review. They should be moved into Extended Data figures because they bear on the central claim.
concerns.quote: Move the heating analysis and the cited Figs. S2 and S7 into ED figures, since they bear on the central claim.

concerns.concern: The field history and cooling protocol (field-cooled or not) before each dataset are not stated, nor whether results depend on them.
concerns.quote: State the field history and cooling protocol (field-cooled or not) before each dataset, and whether results depend on it.

concerns.concern: For Fig. 4h, the meaning of 'effective resistivity' for nonlinear ac data is unclear. It is not stated whether the ac excitation could itself write or erase the state.
concerns.quote: State whether the ac excitation amplitude could itself act as a write or erase stimulus.

concerns.concern: Fig. 4e calls the 15° profile 'very similar' to 0°, yet it terminates near 12 T rather than 18 T; this needs comment.
concerns.quote: The 15° profile is called "very similar" to 0°, yet it terminates near ~12 T rather than ~18 T.

concerns.concern: Terminology is loose: 'minimise entropy' should be free energy, and 'pinning forces between vortices' should be vortex–defect pinning. Calling an effect explained by enhanced disorder pinning 'intrinsic' needs explanation.
concerns.quote: Explain why an effect explained by enhanced disorder pinning is called "intrinsic".

concerns.concern: Units and labels are inconsistent: the ED Fig. 1a axis is in ms instead of A cm⁻², ED Fig. 5b uses s⁻¹ versus ms⁻¹ elsewhere, and Fig. 3b uses J_ext instead of J_ex.
concerns.quote: ED Fig. 1a x-axis reads "J_ex (ms)"; it should be A cm⁻².

concerns.concern: Methods contain a typo ('π = 0' should be φ = 0) and cite the wrong Extended Data Fig. 2 panels.
concerns.quote: "global minimum at π = 0" should read φ = 0.

concerns.concern: References 26 and 57 are duplicates.
concerns.quote: Refs. 26 and 57 are duplicates.

concerns.concern: The text on p. 9 says the effect persists up to the SC1→SC2 boundary just below 20 T in S2. This contradicts ED Fig. 8 and Fig. 4e and should be corrected.
concerns.quote: This is inconsistent with ED Fig. 8 and Fig. 4e.
